convertibility_reason: Uses iCustom indicator 'i-AMMA' which is not a built-in MT5 indicator, and depends on external TradeAlgorithms.mqh library for position sizing and trade execution logic

derived_values.name: TimeShiftSec - bar duration in seconds for signal timestamp
min_rates_total - minimum bars required for indicator calculation

other_exits: Buy closed when i-AMMA[SignalBar+1] > i-AMMA[SignalBar+2] (downtrend detected)
Sell closed when i-AMMA[SignalBar+1] < i-AMMA[SignalBar+2] (uptrend detected)

position_sizing.conditional_logic: MarginMode enum controls sizing: LOT=fixed lots at MM value; BALANCE/FREEMARGIN=fraction of balance/free margin at MM value; LOSSBALANCE/LOSSFREEMARGIN=fraction considering floating loss

custom_logic_notes: Entry uses 3-bar i-AMMA comparison: Value[2] vs Value[1] determines trend direction, Value[0] vs Value[1] confirms momentum continuation for entry. BuyPosOpen/SellPosOpen/SellPosClose/BuyPosClose are boolean gates allowing user to independently enable/disable each direction's entry and exit. Signal timestamp is set to last bar date + bar duration for trade execution. LoadHistory ensures sufficient bar data before signal evaluation.
python_conversion_notes: Custom i-AMMA indicator logic must be replicated in Python since it is loaded via iCustom. The TradeAlgorithms.mqh functions (BuyPositionOpen, SellPositionOpen, BuyPositionClose, SellPositionClose, GlobalVariableDel_, LoadHistory, CIsNewBar) must all be reimplemented. The MarginMode enum with 5 modes requires careful money management logic porting. Signal logic uses 3 consecutive buffer values at offset SignalBar, comparing bar+2 vs bar+1 for trend and bar vs bar+1 for momentum - this is straightforward to replicate with numpy/pandas rolling calculations once the AMMA formula is known.
